findings.where: y 1080-1330, between the 'noor needs a lot  Thu 3 Sep 17:27' strip and the 'left the key under the pot' note
findings.what: In the hero artifact for this category a full-width, note-sized card renders completely blank - no words, no timestamp, no author, no state marker - and the scene that produced it is the only scene in the whole capture that failed: logs/13_messenger_states.json reports ok:false with problems:["pageerror: "].
findings.why: A message that renders as an empty box, on the one screen whose entire job is to prove that message state can be trusted, is exactly the failure the rubric row calls out; a person who sees a blank row in their thread cannot tell a retracted message from a broken one, and that is a reason to open Instagram.
findings.root_cause: The scene's own report names event 0001M4ZQQ0H0PPVTKMMQEE268D as visible on stock graph_01 with tear mask tear_051, but 13_messenger_states.surfaces.json contains neither graph_01 nor tear_051 anywhere - on or off screen - so neither the paper nor the tear was ever drawn for it. The card's interior pixel standard deviation is 7.2/4.9/2.8 against 28-65 for every note around it, i.e. a flat CSS fill with a drop shadow and straight cut edges standing in for a paper surface. The empty pageerror string in the same log strongly suggests an uncaught exception in that row's render path aborted both its surface and its content.
findings.correction: Reproduce the capture of scene 13 with the page error surfaced (the log records an empty message - capture error.message and error.stack), fix the throw in the row that binds event 0001M4ZQQ0H0PPVTKMMQEE268D to a paper stock, and add an assertion to the capture harness that every id in report.visible has a matching paper asset and tear mask in the surfaces list, so a note that renders with no surface fails the run instead of passing it.

findings.where: the right-hand column, the three tall ruled cards dated 23 Aug 26, 18 Aug 26 and 8 Aug 26
findings.what: Three consecutive archive tiles render as large ruled cards that are empty except for a date - interleaved in the same column with photo tiles and voice-note tiles (21s, 47s) that render correctly.
findings.why: It shows the blank-card render of finding 1 is not an isolated accident on one screen but a systemic failure that also reaches the year-deep archive, which is the searchable history this row is judged on; three dated blanks in one column is what a person scrolling their own archive would actually see.
findings.root_cause: Same empty-card path as finding 1 - measured interiors of std 7.8-16.2 against 59-80 for the photo tiles beside them, so no media and no text was painted into the tile, only the ruled paper and the date. Either a media/poster blob that never resolved (04_moments waited 2812 ms on blobs before the shot) or an event type the grid has no renderer for.
findings.correction: Give the archive tile an explicit render for every event type it can be handed, and a visible, named fallback (not a blank) for any tile whose media has not resolved; then assert in the capture that no tile in 04_moments has an interior variance below the paper-grain floor.

findings.where: the state markers beneath each note
findings.what: 'edited' and 'taken back' are two of the five states 13_messenger_states.png exists to show, and neither appears anywhere: the artifact shows read, going, waiting to send, a named failure with retry and a typing line, but the string 'edited' occurs in zero of the eleven text sidecars in the set, and no retraction stub carries a label.
findings.why: The row requires editing and deleting to be present and dependable; reliability.json proves both in the engine ('edited text shown on the host, original kept in the log', 'the row became a stub on the host') but there is no evidence anywhere that either state is legible to the person holding the phone, and the only candidate for a retraction stub is the unlabelled blank card of finding 1.
findings.root_cause: The staged scene for 13 sets up delivery, read, waiting and failure but never stages an edited message or a retracted one, so two of the five states the scene is named for were never put on screen.
findings.correction: Extend the stage step in scene 13 to include one edited message carrying an 'edited' mark (and a way to see the original, since the engine keeps it) and one retracted message rendered as a labelled stub - 'taken back', on paper, with its timestamp - so a retraction is never indistinguishable from a render failure.

findings.artifact: logs/*.json (cold_ms in every scene log) and frames.json
findings.subsystem: cold start over the year-deep history
findings.where: time from page load to the app being ready
findings.what: Every scene backed by the seeded year of history takes 10.9-12.3 s to become ready (02_chat 11663 ms, 13_messenger_states 11282 ms, 11_chat_scroll 10903 ms, 12_search 11948 ms, 01_pulse 12327 ms), while the three scenes with no history are ready in 1259-1321 ms (10_first_run 1263 ms, 17_setup_pwa 1321 ms, 08_state_propagating 1259 ms).
findings.why: That is ten seconds of every cold open spent loading 14,000 events, and it is the rubric's 'spinner that outstays its welcome' measured directly - a person who wants to send one line and gets an eleven-second wait opens the other app, and no artifact in the set shows what is on screen during those ten seconds.
findings.root_cause: The whole event log is loaded and laid out before the app declares ready, rather than the tail of the thread being rendered first and the rest hydrated behind it. The clean first-run number proves the cost is the history, not the shell.
findings.correction: Render and declare ready on the last screenful of the thread, hydrate the rest of the log lazily behind it, and add a cold_ms ceiling to the capture that fails the run - the number is already recorded in every scene log, nothing enforces it.

findings.where: reliability.json top-level 'transport', its 'tailscale.later_check', and the 'link' field of every scene report
findings.what: The capability matrix that proves send, ack, read, reply, react, edit, delete, voice, video, viewer, search, draft survival, kill-mid-send, retry, refusal, offline queue, reconnect ordering and host-offline outbox was run with transport 'local' on 127.0.0.1:42235; the tailnet cross-check inside it is dated 2026-09-05, fifteen days before this capture, and its re-run at capture time is 'pending - the nodes were not answering' (coldstart.json carries the identical stale-and-pending pair), and 13 of the 14 captured scenes report link:'connecting', only 08_state_propagating reaching 'connected'.
findings.why: The rubric explicitly asks whether the transport reliability.json names is the one the build actually runs on, and it is not: every dependability claim in this category is currently proven over loopback, and no still in the set shows a connected peer, so the delivery and read markers in 02_chat and 13_messenger_states are being drawn from staged state rather than from a live link.
findings.root_cause: The two userspace tailscaled daemons were not answering when the capture ran, so the harness fell back to the local transport and kept the dated tailnet result rather than recording the fallback as a gap in the matrix.
findings.correction: Re-run the capability matrix end to end over the tailscale transport and stamp each capability with the transport it was proven on; if the daemons will not come up, mark the affected capabilities unproven for that run instead of reporting all_ok:true beside a transport of 'local'. Separately, stage at least one still with link:'connected' so the markers are shown against a live peer.

findings.where: the photo frame at rect [37, 185, 1365, 1808], and the whole viewer chrome
findings.what: The viewer shows one photo with a caption and a 'PUT IT BACK' close, and nothing else - no next or previous, no position in the set, no date on the image - and the image's own source is 825x1100 drawn at 1344x1792, a 1.63x upscale whose softness reads as a flat, horizontally banded grey across the top 400 px (interior std ~2.5).
findings.why: The row names the media viewer as a capability; a viewer you cannot move through means going back to the thread and hunting for the next photo, and a visibly soft photograph is the thing a person opens the other app to avoid.
findings.root_cause: The viewer is a single-item overlay over the chat rather than a pager over the media set, and the photo it is handed is below the device's own pixel dimensions, so it is upscaled to fit.
findings.correction: Make the viewer a pager over the same filtered media set the archive uses, with the item's date and its position in the set; and serve the viewer an image at least as large as the device's logical viewport times its DPR rather than upscaling the thread's copy.

findings.where: the system strip reading "you's phone …  Wed 22 Apr · 07:09"
findings.what: A possessive template is applied to the second person, producing "you's phone" in the live thread.
findings.why: It is a small thing that appears in the dense history a person scrolls every day, and logs/strings.json reports 114 strings read with zero findings, so the string check does not catch it.
findings.root_cause: The event-line template interpolates <name>'s without a case for the viewer's own name being rendered as 'you'.
findings.correction: Give the template a second-person form ('your phone') and add a rule to the strings check that flags "you's" and any possessive built on a pronoun.

findings.what: Seven notes are on screen where the brief's own floor is eight, which is why MANIFEST.json files this artifact under 'missing' despite it being present and fully measurable at 4.7 MB.
findings.why: Noting it once for the record; per the owner's standing instruction of 2026-09-19 this is demo density rather than a defect a person would hit, and I have not scored it - the thread itself is populated (logs/02_chat.report.json records 14,062 events behind it) and legible.
findings.root_cause: The scroll position for the shot lands where the notes are tall, so one fewer fits.
findings.correction: Move the scroll target a few hundred pixels, or lower the floor in the brief - a bookkeeping fix, not a product one.

findings.what: Neither artifact exists: with no /dev/kvm the x86_64 image runs under QEMU instruction emulation, adbd answered after 113 minutes but the framework never came up, so no APK could be installed and no second screen existed.
findings.why: Recorded once, as the rubric instructs. The consequence for this category is that the Android half of 'one Android app and one installable PWA' is unmeasured - every capability in this row is evidenced from the WebKit PWA only - not that the build is penalised again for a container limitation it documented and measured rather than faked.
findings.root_cause: Hardware: no KVM in this container.
findings.correction: Nothing to correct here; capture these two on a machine with /dev/kvm or on a real handset, and until then say plainly in the evidence set that the messenger capabilities are proven on the PWA side only.

what_is_working: The reliability matrix in reliability.json is the strongest thing in this category and should not be disturbed: 175 events on both sides, 0 duplicates, monotonic gapless ordering (seq 1..174) across two injected offline/online cycles, 26 events queued offline and every one delivered on reconnect, a kill mid-send that the host received exactly once with the retry not duplicating it, a draft and its pairing intact after the client process was closed and reopened, and a host-offline outbox that delivered with its sequence intact. That is a real answer to 'no dropped or duplicated messages, no lost drafts, correct ordering after going offline and reconnecting'.

The failure row in 13_messenger_states.png is better than what it is replacing: 'it would not go ✗ / the other phone couldn't read it. / ↻ try again' names the reason in plain language on the note itself and offers the retry in place, and reliability.json's refusal_reported confirms the host answers for an event it will not take rather than dropping it out of the reply. Keep this exactly as it is.

Delivery state is spelled in words, not icons alone - 'read ✓✓', 'going', 'waiting to send' - each legible at full resolution beneath its own note, and shown only on the sender's own messages in 02_chat.png and 11_chat_scroll.mp4. The 'noor writing…' typing line is present and readable.

The dense scroll is clean: 330 frames at 60 fps over a 14,000-event history with 1 repeated frame (0.3 %), a longest still run of 1 frame, 0 brightness jumps and mean change per frame of 0.043, and the strip bears the numbers out - content differs in every panel, nothing blanks during the fling, and timestamps run in order across a day boundary (21:58 → 22:00 → 06:35 → 06:40 → 07:09). There is no scroll jank here.

Search in 12_search.png is a real full-text search over the year with the term highlighted in the hits and facets for kind, person and time, and reliability.json shows it returning hits across all nine event types including photo, video, voice_note, feeling and the shared-life modules.

Reactions fold onto their target note as a small object rather than becoming a row of their own (visible on 'Then I dreamed a better film…' and 'There was a boat.' in 11_chat_scroll.mp4), which matches reliability.json's react result.

10_first_run.png is a clean, fast empty state - ready in 1263 ms, with 'first one's yours. / whatever it is. it only goes to one person.' and no spinner, no marketing voice and no engagement machinery.
verdict: Underneath this is a messenger whose engine is genuinely well built and honestly measured - gapless ordering after two disconnections, no duplicate on a kill mid-send, a draft that survives a restart, an offline queue that drains in order, and a failed send that says why and offers to try again - and a dense scroll with effectively zero dropped frames over fourteen thousand events. But the one scene in the entire capture that failed is this category's own hero: 13_messenger_states.json reports ok:false with an uncaught page error, and the picture it produced contains a note-sized card with nothing in it, no paper and no tear, the same empty-card render that appears three more times in the archive; on top of that the app takes eleven seconds to open on the real history against 1.3 seconds when it is empty, two of the five states the hero exists to show never appear at all, and the whole capability matrix was proven over loopback with the tailnet check fifteen days stale and un-rerunnable. A blank message row and an eleven-second cold open are each, on their own, a reason to open Instagram instead, so the rubric's own clause applies and this scores below its floor.
